data.title: Mergers and acquisitions
data.description:
The following bids, mergers, acquisitions and disposals were reported by 1510 GMT on Friday:

** Czech investment group AKIPIA has agreed to acquire leading car locks systems maker Kiekert.

** Deutsche Boerse secured unconditional EU antitrust approval for its €5.35 billion ($5.87 billion) acquisition of fund-trading platform Allfunds after regulators said the deal raised no competition concerns.

** Brazilian energy and commodities company Raizen is considering the sale of its fuel distribution arm as part of a broader divestment plan, founding shareholder Rubens Ometto told Reuters.

** A banking syndicate led by Kazakhstan's largest bank, Halyk , has raised $1.5 billion to fund private investor Central Asia Resources Holding Ltd's acquisition of Kazakh gold miner Altynalmas (ALMS.KZ), Halyk said.

** Offers the Belgian government has received for a 20% stake in state-owned bank Belfius have been too low, Finance Minister Jan Jambon told the parliament.

** Shares of Japan Tobacco jumped on the prospect of the company joining hands with Altria to acquire, and split up, British cigarette maker Imperial Brands in a potential multibillion-dollar deal.

** Tesla has submitted plans to acquire German manufacturing systems supplier EMAG, which also makes parts for humanoid robots, a filing with Germany's antitrust authority showed.

** French laser technology company Lumibird said it had entered into exclusive talks with defence group Thales for the sale of a 51.6% stake held by its CEO and majority shareholder Marc Le Flohic.

** Infrastructure investor I Squared Capital is in advanced talks to buy German outdoor advertising group Stroeer , reviving discussions that stalled earlier this year, according to two people familiar with the matter.

** German automotive and industrial supplier Schaeffler has sold a 6.5% stake in its Indian unit, generating net proceeds of more than €300 million ($330 million), its CEO told Reuters on Thursday.

** Seed group Vilmorin has entered exclusive talks to buy French rival Lidea to strengthen its position in Europe's crop seed market, Vilmorin's parent company said on Thursday.

** Italy's Banco Desio has agreed to buy an 85.3% majority stake in Cassa di Risparmio di Orvieto from Banca del Mezzogiorno for about €124 million ($136 million), the two lenders said in a joint press release on Thursday.

data.title: BAE Systems Secures $6 Billion in Combat-Vehicle Contracts For Several European Nations — Update
data.description:
By Mauro Orru

BAE Systems said it had secured $6 billion in contracts to supply hundreds of combat vehicles to several European nations as they seek to buttress their armed forces amid high geopolitical tensions.

The U.K. arms maker said it would deliver more than 400 CV90 combat vehicles to the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, Finland and Lithuania under contracts awarded through separate purchase-order agreements.

The group said the procurement included support systems, training, spare parts, special tools and test equipment and that the vehicles and components would be produced through a distributed supplier network across those nations.

An order of this magnitude is a major boost to BAE Systems, and a sign that defense spending in Europe remains healthy following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Members of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization have expedited plans to rearm since then, placing a steady stream of orders with BAE Systems and other defense groups to shore up their forces.

Over the summer, the U.K. government said it would commit 15 billion pounds ($19.66 billion) in additional funding for its armed forces, raising investments that London had earmarked for defense over the next four years to about 298 billion pounds.

Aside from combat vehicles, BAE Systems provides ammunition, missile launchers and artillery systems, including the M777 howitzer that Ukraine has employed widely in its fight against Russia. It also provides cybersecurity services, electronic warfare and night-vision systems, surveillance and reconnaissance sensors.

Chief Executive Charles Woodburn said earlier this month that order momentum remained positive, with orders up to 33 billion pounds by then from more than 27 billion pounds a year earlier. The company raised its free cash flow projection for the second time this year, projecting about 3 billion pounds that included some benefits from customer advances it had received to date.

While orders keep growing, BAE Systems is seeking to better position itself in a market where contractors fight fiercely for a slice of defense spending from governments. Last week, the group said it was looking at options to shed up to 1,070 roles in its head office and air division in the U.K. in an effort to make its operations leaner and more competitive.

data.description:

Marula Mining PLC

("Marula" or the "Company")

27 November 2026

Expanded Mandate with AcaciaCap Advisors

Marula Mining PLC (AQSE: MARU | A2X:MAR), an African-focused mining and development company, announces that it has expanded its existing corporate finance mandates with AcaciaCap Advisors Proprietary Limited ("AcaciaCap"), to include a proposed primary listing of its shares on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange and to also include non-exclusive advisory support for ore sales, offtake agreements and related financings in respect to its critical minerals mines and development projects in South and East Africa.

Proposed Listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange

AcaciaCap has been formally engaged to advise and assist the Company with a proposed primary listing in the General Segment of the Main Board of JSE Limited ("JSE") (“JSE Listing Mandate”).

Under the JSE Listing Engagement, AcaciaCap will provide the following services: preparation of the Pre-Listing Statement, listing application and required announcements, assistance with external-company registration and exchange control approval, and coordination of the listing process.

Fees and expenses under the JSE Listing Engagement are considered standard for an engagement of this nature.

No capital raising is associated with the proposed listing. A separate capital raising is envisaged during 2027, but its amount and terms have not been specified and funding has not been secured under the mandate.

AcaciaCap, already the Company’s A2X Markets sponsor, will also act as post-listing sponsor under the accepted listing mandate.

Members of the Company’s executive management team are scheduled to meet with representatives from the JSE in Johannesburg.

The proposed primary listing on the JSE remains subject to applicable JSE requirements and approvals, with the timetable and commencement date to be agreed. Acceptance of the JSE Listing Engagement with AcaciaCap does not confirm listing approval.

Offtake and Financing Advisory

AcaciaCap has also been formally engaged to assist the Company on a non-exclusive basis with ore sales, offtake agreements and related financing, including engagement with prospective buyers and funders.

Fees and commissions under these agreements are considered standard for agreements of this nature, and only become payable once transactions are completed and any sales proceeds or funding advances are deposited into the Company’s bank account.

By Karen Brettell

Improving risk appetite on Friday bolstered risk-sensitive currencies including the Australian dollar, while the US dollar was on track for a modest weekly gain.

Wall Street's main indexes opened higher on Friday, with the Nasdaq poised to outperform as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday break and rushed back into battered AI-linked shares. Efforts by China to shore up its stock market also boosted sentiment.

"A dip-buying recovery in tech stocks is lifting risk appetite across markets," said Elias Haddad, global head of markets strategy at Brown Brothers Harriman.

The US currency has benefited from safe-haven demand from volatile equity markets, but it is also sensitive to capital flows to the AI trade, which has made it difficult at times to parse market moves.

“FX markets have shaken off their fixation on energy markets, replacing it, for now, with a focus on equities,” said Daragh Maher, head of digital assets research and senior FX strategist at HSBC.

“This creates a headache. The USD’s relationship with equities is unreliable, caught between its safe-haven role and its appeal as a proxy for US exceptionalism. The same equity signal could prompt very different FX responses,” he said.

The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, rose 0.11% to 103.89, with the euro down 0.14% at $1.0952. The greenback is on course for a weekly gain of around 0.6%.

The Australian dollar strengthened 0.27% versus the greenback to $0.665, recovering from an almost one-year low reached on Wednesday.

FED TO CONTINUE HIKING

With US growth remaining strong and inflation still elevated, traders are pricing in continued rate hikes from the Federal Reserve, which has also supported the US currency.

Fed funds futures traders are pricing in 99% odds of a hike in December and a 64% chance of an additional increase in January.

Key data releases next week, including November’s jobs report, will be evaluated for further clues on likely Fed policy.

DOLLAR/YEN 160 LEVEL BACK IN FOCUS

Against the Japanese yen , the dollar strengthened 0.13% to 159.46, amid concerns about another round of Japanese intervention.

Data showed that annual core inflation in Tokyo accelerated in November at the fastest pace in 16 months, bolstering the case for an interest rate hike as soon as next month.

"The yen is understandably weaker today given the strong rebound in risk that has helped lift US Treasury bond yields," said Derek Halpenny, strategist at MUFG. "Better risk conditions could quickly bring back focus on intervention, especially if we get a hawkish hike from the FOMC on December 9."

In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 0.94% to $60,192.

data.title: EU policy goals raise funding, implementation questions
data.description:
By Cian Muenster

After years of proposing ambitious plans to green the economy, sharpen competitiveness and deepen integration, the European Union is now increasingly confronting questions on how those goals will be funded, implemented and enforced.

The answers could shape the EU's next seven-year budget, which is currently under negotiation, and determine whether the bloc can implement stated policies on a range of issues, including climate adaptation, labour mobility and energy efficiency.

The EU's proposed 2028-2034 Multiannual Financial Framework has sparked debates around common EU spending, with the European Commission pushing to streamline expenditure through National and Regional Partnership Plans, while some lawmakers say the changes could weaken parliamentary oversight.

Earlier this month, Parliament co-rapporteur Siegfried Muresan warned lawmakers would not support a budget which turned common EU spending into "27 separate national agendas".

The German Foreign Ministry, however, defended the proposed changes, saying the current system in which more than 90% of EU spending was pre-allocated had repeatedly proved too rigid when new priorities emerged.

CLIMATE ADAPTATION

Meanwhile, critics of a proposed EU Climate Resilience Law have said the initiative lacks dedicated funding, despite Commission estimates that climate adaptation investments would need to reach around €70 billion ($76.72 billion) a year.

"Risk assessments alone will not shield communities," senior European Parliament lawmaker Delara Burkhardt told Reuters, warning the law risked becoming a "paper tiger" without ring-fenced funding.

A Commission official, however, said adaptation would form part of the proposed budget's overall 35% green-spending target and would be supported through instruments including National and Regional Partnership Plans, Horizon Europe, the LIFE programme and the proposed European Competitiveness Fund.

The current EU budget already contributes more than €100 billion to climate resilience measures, the official said, adding member states and private investors would also play an important role in financing adaptation.

DELAYS AND PARTICIPATION

Elsewhere, efforts to cut red tape have raised questions about whether member states would follow through.

EU countries this month approved a common digital eDeclaration portal for companies temporarily posting workers abroad, but participation remains voluntary.

Germany's VDMA engineering association warned that limited uptake could end up preserving the patchwork of national reporting requirements that were in force.

Broad participation would be key to the project's success, a Commission official said, adding that participating governments would save money because the Commission would develop and maintain the IT systems.

Questions have also emerged over the pace of implementation in some measures to support broader EU policy goals.

In July, the Commission set an indicative target for electricity to account for 46% of final energy consumption by 2040, estimating the shift could reduce the bloc's fossil-fuel import bill by up to €260 billion a year.

Environmental groups ECOS and CLASP warn, however, that delays to updated ecodesign and energy-labelling rules for heating and cooling equipment risk slowing the electrification needed to achieve those objectives.

"Every day of regulatory delay pushes the electrification of the heating sector further away," said ECOS policy manager Rita Tedesco.

According to the Commission, efficiency measures have saved the bloc €120 billion in fossil fuel imports from the beginning of Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 until July 2026.

"Europe increasingly knows what it needs to do," Fabian Zuleeg, chief executive of the European Policy Centre wrote in a September commentary.

"The challenge is turning ambition into delivery and partnerships into power."

data.title: Dalmia Bharat to buy back shares worth ₹700 crore; sets ₹1,850 price ceiling
data.description:
Dalmia Bharat has approved a share buyback worth up to ₹700 crore through the open market at a maximum price of ₹1,850 per equity share.

The company's board approved the buyback at a meeting held on November 23. The offer will cover fully paid-up equity shares with a face value of ₹2 each, excluding shares held by promoters, promoter group members and persons in control.

The company will buy back shares at a price of up to ₹1,850 apiece, with the total buyback amount capped at ₹700 crore, excluding related expenses.

The buyback will open on or before December 2, 2026. Once it opens, Dalmia Bharat will place buy orders through its broker on the stock exchanges' normal trading segment, purchasing shares at or below the maximum buyback price.

The company has said it will utilise at least 75% of the maximum buyback size, or ₹525 crore, towards the buyback. It will also deploy at least 40% of the maximum amount, or ₹280 crore, during the first half of the 66 working days from the buyback's opening date.

Promoters, promoter group members and persons in control will not participate in the buyback, the company said in its exchange filing.

Dalmia Bharat has constituted a buyback committee to oversee the process and appointed Company Secretary and Compliance Officer Rajeev Kumar as the compliance officer for the buyback.

According to the company's September 2026 shareholding pattern, promoters and the promoter group held 55.84% of Dalmia Bharat, while public shareholders owned 44.16%. Mutual funds held 15.59% and foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) owned 7.36%.

Dalmia Bharat shares ended 2.78% lower at ₹1,492 on the NSE on Friday, November 27, falling ₹42.70 during the session. The stock has declined 30.16% so far in 2026, shedding ₹644.20 from its previous year-end level.

data.title: Norse Atlantic's Norwegian Operating Unit Declares Bankruptcy
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Norse Atlantic said its Norwegian operating unit has filed for bankruptcy, while the parent company continues efforts to secure short-term financing.

The budget long-haul carrier has been exploring a potential sale, merger or partnership for several months and is currently in talks with investors over a possible takeover that would include a financing solution.

"Despite extensive efforts, the company has so far not been able to secure sufficient funding to meet its short-term liquidity needs," the company said in a statement.

The carrier, which operates two subsidiaries--Norse Atlantic Airways AS and Norse Atlantic U.K.--said Friday that the board of Norse Atlantic Airways AS has concluded there is no longer a basis for continued operations.

Earlier in the day, Norse Atlantic said the lessors of its entire fleet of 12 Boeing 787 Dreamliners had moved to terminate their leasing agreements.

"The board, management and advisers of the listed entity Norse Atlantic ASA and the UK subsidiary are working to find a solution for the remaining part of the business to continue operations," said Norse Atlantic Chief Executive Eivind Roald.

All Norse flights have been canceled and ticket sales have been discontinued. A message on its website warns passengers not to travel to airports for canceled flights, adding that customer service is no longer available by phone, email, chat or social media.

data.title: SemiLEDs Reports Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year End 2026 Financial Results
data.description:
SemiLEDs Corporation (), “SemiLEDs” or the “Company,” a developer and manufacturer of LED chips and LED components, today announced its financial results for the fourth quarter and full fiscal year 2026, ended August 31, 2026.

Revenue for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was $6.4 million, compared to $9.1 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2026. GAAP net income attributable to SemiLEDs stockholders for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was $640 thousand, or $0.08 per diluted share, compared to a net income of $1.5 million, or $0.18 per diluted share, in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.

GAAP gross margin for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 decreased to 23%, compared to 27% for the third quarter of fiscal 2026. Operating margin for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 decreased to 7%, compared to 16% for the third quarter of fiscal 2026. The Company’s cash and cash equivalents were $4.6 million at August 31, 2026, compared to $6.0 million at the end of the third quarter of fiscal 2026.

Revenues for fiscal year 2026 decreased to $19.1 million, compared to $43.0 million in fiscal year 2025. GAAP net income attributable to SemiLEDs stockholders for fiscal year 2026 was $817 thousand, or $0.10 per diluted share, compared to a net loss of $1.1 million, or $(0.15) per diluted share, in fiscal year 2025.

GAAP gross margin for fiscal year 2026 increased to 21%, compared to 6% for fiscal year 2025. Operating margin for fiscal year 2026 was 0.1%, compared to negative 4% in fiscal year 2025. The Company’s cash and cash equivalents were $4.6 million as of August 31, 2026, compared to $2.6 million as of August 31, 2025.

In fiscal years 2026 and 2025, the Company entered into a number of buy-sell orders for equipment that it purchased and then sold to its customers, and the Company anticipates continuing to receive buy-sell purchase orders in fiscal year 2027. As a result of these purchase orders and the associated uncertainty of the business, the Company’s revenue, cost of revenues, receivables, inventories and customer deposits may vary significantly over future quarters.

About SemiLEDs

SemiLEDs develops, manufactures, and sells light emitting diode (LED) chips, LED components, LED modules, sensor components incorporating LED or vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL), and systems. Its products are used for general lighting and specialty industrial applications, including ultraviolet, or UV, curing of polymers, LED light therapy in medical/cosmetic applications, counterfeit detection, germicidal and virucidal devices, LED lighting for horticulture applications, architectural lighting, entertainment lighting, and sensing of pressure or distance using LED or VCSEL.
